title: Token-bucket epoch rollback triggering intermittent customer traffic blackouts
creator: Anika Desai
description:
Summary:
A serialization regression introduced during an epoch-state refactor can cause persisted token-bucket state to roll back to a prior epoch under leader-restart edge conditions. When rollback happens at scale this leads the admission layer to believe tenants have more available credits than they should, which in turn causes the orchestrator to aggressively evict warm workers (thinking tokens were consumed elsewhere) or conversely causes sudden credit exhaustion and 429/503s depending on the fallback path.

Affected surfaces:
- Hosted API: manifested as intermittent 429 spikes and short-lived 503s during regional orchestrator leadership changes.
- Dedicated: customers on reserved pools saw rapid cold-start churn and transient capacity blackouts.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): state migration path exposed the bug during rolling updates of the control plane.

Detection and impact:
- First reported by support on 2026-03-03 for two high-usage customers on hosted. Pager alerts fired for tenant_429_rate and orchestrator_eviction_rate.
- Spike correlated to control-plane leader restarts and a scheduled midnight compaction job.
- Customer impact: multiple production customers experienced 5–30s blackouts affecting request success rate; overall platform error budget impacted for the day (SLA-level).

Root cause (summary):
- During a refactor we changed token-bucket epoch persistence to a compressed binary format but introduced a non-atomic write path. Under a leader handover the write could be partially applied and later re-read as an earlier epoch value due to a combination of write reordering and the compaction job restoring older segments. The admission controller reads the epoch and re-applies bucket deltas assuming monotonic advancement; when epoch moves backward the logic incorrectly grants tokens or resets allocator state leading to chaotic eviction/fallback behavior.

Short-term mitigations applied (already in prod):
- Disabled midnight compaction for affected regions (2026-03-04 02:10 UTC).
- Emergency hotfix to make reads tolerant to epoch decreases by clamping and rejecting suspicious state (rollback detector) — pushed to hosted control plane (2026-03-05 06:40 UTC).
- Added tenant-level emergency rate-smoothing at the proxy layer to flatten bursts while we triage.

Planned permanent fix:
1) Make persistence writes atomic using a write-then-rename pattern and add a format-version header to persisted blobs.
2) Add a strict monotonicity check: if epoch decreases, treat as corrupted and consult leader consensus (do not auto-grant tokens).
3) Add a migration script to scan compacted segments and reconcile inconsistent epochs.
4) Add unit/e2e tests simulating leader restarts+partial writes for hosted/dedicated/private.
5) Release behind a feature-flag with staged rollout and automatic rollback on metric regressions.

Rollout plan:
- Merge PR -> internal canary (control plane hosts only) -> 1% traffic for 24h -> 10% for 24h -> 100% for hosted; dedicated/private customers will get opt-in package first for a controlled upgrade.
- Monitoring: new metrics token_bucket_rollback_count, persisted_epoch_mismatch_rate, orchestrator_eviction_rate. Alerts and dashboards are defined in the related doc.

Testing and validation:
- e2e harness added to simulate leader churn under write interleavings.
- Load tests with tenant traffic patterns from the three impacted customers reproduced the spike locally.
- Backfill job will run in staging to validate the migration script on snapshots.

Communications:
- Support templates prepared and sent to affected customers on 2026-03-06.
- Postmortem planned after full rollout; owners: Anika (investigation), Marco (fix), Priya (customer comms).

References:
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/token-bucket-rollback
- Customer tickets: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/HD-9442, https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/DD-1184
